ut_stitches_wall_the.blurb: A small limestone crag in Millcreek Canyon, in the central Wasatch east of Salt Lake City. The rock is a thin, fin-shaped projection with sharp texture, so expect rough holds and tender skin. All 11 routes are bolted sport lines, with one at 5.9, most in the 5.10 range and a handful at 5.11. The lines are short, which makes it a quick stop for a pair of climbers who want a few pitches without a big day. It tends to be quiet compared with the busier canyon walls nearby.

ut_shoreline_crag.blurb: An overhanging conglomerate sport crag high on the left side of City Creek Canyon, in the central Wasatch above Salt Lake City. The wall is built around two large cave-like features, and the bolts are a mix of glue-ins and mechanicals on generally solid rock. This is a steep, strenuous place with 11 sport routes, almost all 5.11 and 5.12, one around 5.10 and one 5.13. It suits climbers comfortable on hard, powerful lines rather than anyone looking for warm-ups.

ut_house_party_boulder.blurb: A single large freestanding boulder beside the road in Buckhorn Wash, part of the San Rafael Swell in central Utah. It holds 11 problems with a hard-leaning spread: a few moderate lines around V2 to V4, then a cluster from V6 to V8 and a V9 traverse at the top end. Besides face lines it offers a sit start, a traverse and a jump problem. It is an easy one-boulder stop rather than a full day of circuits, and good for climbers already pushing into the harder grades.

ut_millie_boulder.blurb: A single boulder in the Brighton Boulders zone at the head of Big Cottonwood Canyon, in Utah's central Wasatch, sitting near the Millie lift at roughly 8,700 feet. The 11 problems skew hard: one easy V1, then a V6, a pair of V7s, a V8, two V9s, two V10s and two V11s. Being high in an alpine setting, it is a summer-and-early-fall stop. It is best for strong boulderers, with only a single gentle problem for anyone warming up.

ut_shame_wall_the.blurb: A sport wall above the Grey Cliffs Picnic Area in American Fork Canyon, southern Wasatch. The left side feels like a gym wall outdoors: slightly short of vertical beneath a roof, with bolts close at hand on both sides. Farther right the lines get harder to tell apart, and a roof crossing sits near the middle. There are 11 sport routes, mostly 5.10 with a few at 5.11 and one 5.12. The wall picks up late-afternoon shade in summer, and gets midday sun in early spring and late fall.

ut_29th_street.blurb: A small southwest-facing crag in a quiet side canyon above Ogden, with views over the city. It stays in shade in the morning and gets sun through the afternoon and evening. The 11 routes are mostly bolted sport lines plus a couple of trad lines, and several can be top-roped, with a small roof breaking up the wall. Grades run from an easy 5.5 through a few 5.8s and 5.9s, with 5.10 the most common and one 5.11. It sees less traffic than the busier Ogden crags, and suits newer leaders and mixed groups.
